mechanism_narrative: A higher current value of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation expectations, which typically lead to reduced equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above the 50th percentile of its historical range, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.5% signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5.5, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A tightening labor market, indicated by a monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% and a monthly decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.3%, signals inflationary pressure that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), a positive quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0 and GDPC1 growth is positive, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower current value of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO is below the 50th percentile of its historical range, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1500 (thousands) signals a weakening housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 1500, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market imbalance, indicated by a monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 0.5% and a monthly decrease in residential sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5%, signals economic stress that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), a positive quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0 and GDPC1 growth is positive, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
